title: Real-Time Social Listening: What 10 Vendors Document (2026)
summary: Real-time social listening means four different things. See what 10 vendors document about update speed by plan and source (October 2026) and how to test it.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** In 2026, "real-time" in social listening can mean anything from X's documented stream latency of roughly 4-5 seconds (P99) to an entry plan that updates every 12 hours (Sources:[X API docs, 2026](https://docs.x.com/x-api/posts/filtered-stream/introduction) ;[Brand24](https://brand24.com/prices/) ,[Mentionlytics](https://www.mentionlytics.com/pricing/) and[SentiOne](https://sentione.com/pricing) pricing pages, October 2026). Vendors document collection cadence, ingestion latency, dashboard update frequency and alert latency separately, and most publish only some of them. Before you buy real-time social listening, ask which clock you are getting, and on which plan.


Four vendors in this review list a 12-hour or daily refresh and a "real-time" or "continuous" tier on the same pricing page. They are not contradicting themselves. They sell different plans under one word.


That is the problem with real-time social listening in 2026: the term has no standard definition. A vendor can mean how often it polls a source, how fast a post appears, how often your dashboard refreshes or how fast an alert reaches you. If you buy on the word alone, you may buy a refresh interval.


This post maps what 10 vendors document about update speed, what platform APIs allow underneath them, and how to test the claim yourself. For the strategic difference between[real-time and historical listening](https://syncly.app/blog/real-time-and-historical-social-listening) , start with our earlier guide. Here, the word itself is the subject.


## What does real-time social listening actually mean?


Vendors use "real-time" for four different things, and a fifth, the platform floor, caps all four.


**Collection cadence** : how often the tool polls, crawls or receives data from each source.


**Ingestion latency** : the time from publication to appearance in the product.


**Dashboard update frequency** : how often your project or dashboard refreshes, which many vendors tie to your plan.


**Alert latency** : the time from an event to a notification reaching you.


**Platform floor** : the lowest delay a platform's own access allows. No vendor can beat it, but a vendor can undershoot it by plan design.


A vendor can document one of these well and stay silent on the rest. That is the pattern below.


## What do platform APIs allow, regardless of the vendor?


Platform access sets the floor, and only X documents a streaming path with a latency figure.


-


**X:** X documents that the Filtered Stream delivers posts "within seconds of publication" and cites approximately 4-5 seconds of P99 latency. X documents access as pay-per-use and Enterprise. (Source:[X API docs, 2026](https://docs.x.com/x-api/posts/filtered-stream/introduction) )


-


**Meta (Instagram):** The hashtag endpoint returns only media published in the last 24 hours and caps you at 30 unique hashtags per 7 days. Webhooks cover comments and mentions on accounts connected to your app. The webhooks page does not mention hashtag search. (Source:[Meta hashtag docs, 2026](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-api/reference/ig-hashtag/recent-media) ;[Meta webhooks docs, 2026](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/webhooks) )


-


**TikTok:** The research API serves archived data, new videos take up to 48 hours to appear, and the program is not open to commercial users. Commercial tools would need other routes, which that page does not describe. We do not guess what they are. (Source:[TikTok Research API FAQ, 2026](https://developers.tiktok.com/doc/research-api-faq) )


-


**YouTube:** Push notifications cover channel feeds: uploads and title or description updates. Keyword discovery is not a push source in the docs, and Google gives no latency figure beyond "near real-time". (Source:[YouTube push notifications guide, 2026](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/guides/push_notifications) )


Meta's 24-hour window is why backfill is its own question. See our guide to[historical data backfill costs](https://syncly.app/blog/historical-data-backfill-costs-for-social-listening-in-2026) .

Four vendors tier-gate the label. Brand24, Mentionlytics, SentiOne and BrandMentions each document a 12-hour or daily refresh on an entry plan and "real-time" or "continuous" on a top plan. Same product, same word, different clock.


X documents a stream within seconds, so on X a 12-hour interval would be a plan setting rather than an API requirement. We do not know whether these vendors use X's stream.


Only four vendors publish a latency or collection-time figure: Sprinklr and Emplifi per source, YouScan as a range, and Meltwater for alerts. Of the other six, Brand24 gives only a qualitative phrase and five publish none. Brand24, Mentionlytics, BrandMentions and SentiOne do document refresh intervals by plan.


**Real-time with no number.** Determ and Awario document no interval or latency. Brandwatch Consumer Research, Hootsuite (Talkwalker) and Mention also use real-time language, and we found no number for them on the pages we opened. Sprout Social's features page gives no cadence or latency wording, and its help article returned an error when we tried it. Read those as "could not confirm", not "not published".


**Emplifi's Facebook trap.** Emplifi documents new Facebook mentions at up to 1 hour. The "every 4 hours" figure in the same table is the refresh interval for post metrics on existing posts. Read the column header before the number. (Source:[Emplifi docs, 2026](https://docs.emplifi.io/platform/latest/home/downloading-and-processing-listening-data) )


**Meltwater's clock.** The 2-5 minutes starts at detection, not publication. Meltwater's own help page says the delay between publication and indexing depends on the source, and it publishes no number for it. (Source:[Meltwater community help, 2026](https://community.meltwater.com/meltwater-product-answers-428/meltwater-alerts-11542) )


**BrandMentions' three statements.** The pricing page lists daily, hourly and realtime updates by plan, and the homepage promises real-time alerts. The help center says projects refresh once per day by default and that real-time monitoring sits on higher-tier plans, without naming them. These may all hold on different plans, but together they do not say which plan gets what. (Source:[BrandMentions help center, 2026](https://help.brandmentions.com/en/articles/12637878-what-are-the-project-limits-and-how-often-is-data-updated) )


**Platform routes shape the TikTok numbers.** Emplifi documents new TikTok mentions every 24-48 hours, and Sprinklr documents within 12 to 24 hours. Brandwatch Listen's help center says a connected TikTok account's top 1,000 mentions and performance metrics refresh daily (every 24 hours). Vendors may use different access routes, so this is not a dispute over the truth. (Source:[Brandwatch Listen help center, 2026](https://social-media-management-help.brandwatch.com/en/articles/12767982-sources-for-listen-mentions) )


**Instagram hashtags run into Meta's window.** Meta documents a 24-hour hashtag window, Sprinklr documents 5-60 minutes, and Emplifi documents hashtag search "in real time". Our inference, not a vendor claim: for hashtag search, "real time" can only mean polling a 24-hour window. If you track hashtags, see our review of[Keyhole alternatives for hashtag tracking](https://syncly.app/blog/best-keyhole-alternatives-for-real-time-hashtag-tracking-in-2026) .


## How can a buyer measure ingestion speed before signing?


Measure it with your own posts, on the plan you would buy, and report it as your result rather than the vendor's.


1.


Create a distinct, harmless test token per source (for example "zq-latency-test-0417") so your query matches only your posts.


2.


Publish at least 10 test posts per source on accounts you own, across times of day and weekdays. Record each platform timestamp in UTC. You get a median and a worst case, not one lucky run.


3.


Set up the query on the plan tier you would actually buy. Trials often default to a higher tier, so confirm which.


4.


Poll the feed every 1-5 minutes and log the first time each post appears.


5.


Log the dashboard and each alert channel separately, because the dashboard may show a mention later than the raw feed does. Alert latency is alert arrival minus first appearance. Total is alert arrival minus publication.


6.


Test a brand-new hashtag as well as an old one. A new Instagram hashtag may show nothing older than 24 hours.


7.


Test third-party content too. Owned-account and public-discovery routes can run on different cadences.


8.


Compare your numbers with the documented figures. Report them as "observed in our test on \[date\], on \[plan\]".


Then put four questions to every vendor:


-


What starts the clock: publication, detection or indexing?


-


Which access route does each source use?


-


Does my plan tier change the refresh?


-


How fast do alerts arrive, per channel?

## Key Takeaways


-


"Real-time" covers four different things: collection cadence, ingestion latency, dashboard update frequency and alert latency.


-


Brand24, Mentionlytics, SentiOne and BrandMentions document 12-hour or daily refreshes on entry plans and "real-time" or "continuous" on top plans, as of October 2026.


-


Only four of 10 vendors publish a latency or collection-time figure, and the clock start varies: Meltwater counts from detection, YouScan from publication.


-


Platform floors apply to everyone: X documents seconds, Meta a 24-hour hashtag window, TikTok's research route up to 48 hours.


-


Test on the plan you would buy, with at least 10 posts per source, and report the result as observed in your test.


For four vendors, "real-time" is a plan setting before it is a measurement. The 10 vendors here use one label for four different things, and most document only some of them. So stop asking whether a tool is real-time, and ask which clock, on which plan, from which start point. To put those questions to Syncly Social,[book a demo](https://syncly.app/demo) .
